event: The first thing is weight: a foot presses down onto the ground, and the ground is the core.

memory.fact: The core began the moment a settler's foot first pressed down onto the ground above it.
The Waking Stone, the core, is the story's protagonist and point of view.

event: It has no ears and no eyes; it wakes because it was touched.

memory.fact: The core is blind and has no ears.
The core woke because it was touched.

event: More feet, then wagons grind to a stop above it, and it surfaces out of a bottomless dark.

memory.fact: The core did not wake into a known self, but surfaced out of a bottomless dark.
The settlers arrived by wagon and made camp.
The founding camp is a frontier settlement founded directly above the buried core.

event: It knows itself heavy, cold and down, beneath everything; it does not know its name.

memory.fact: The core is heavy, cold and down: a weight beneath the weight.

event: It reaches for who it was and finds a fraying thread, thin as heat lifting off stone at dusk.

memory.fact: Behind the core's waking trails a fraying thread, thin as the heat that lifts off stone at dusk.
Pulling the thread yields only fragments.

event: In the thread: a different cold, a falling, a hand it reached for and did not close around.

memory.fact: One fragment is a hand the core reached for and did not close around.

event: Pulling frightens it, and in its first hour it learns not to pull too hard.

memory.fact: Pulling at the thread of its past-life memory frightens the core.
In its first hour the core learned not to pull the thread too hard.

event: Settlers come off the stopped wagons in ones and twos; each footfall is the whole world arriving.

memory.fact: The core perceives the world only through touch.
The core feels weight, vibration and pressure through the bound soil that is its body.

event: By day the sun's warmth soaks down and eases it a degree; by night the old cold rises.

memory.fact: The core knows day by the sun's warmth soaking down, and night by the cold rising from below.

event: Rain reaches it last of all, like slow fingers spread flat on its body, gone by morning.

memory.fact: Rain percolates down to the core last of all.

event: It learns the kinds of weight: a wagon's harsh grinding bite under a great load.
A sleeper's weight settles and breathes, a faint tide it finds the most companionable thing.

memory.fact: At night the living lie their weight on the soil, and it breathes, an endless faint tide.

event: That first day a shovel bites into it, cutting a shallow trench for the first stakes.
To be dug into is to be opened, the most personal thing yet; it cannot flinch, and is changed.
When the sun has crossed and the cold come up, it finds the feet do not go on forever.
At one fixed line the feet stop being it; past that line a foot falls and it feels nothing.

memory.fact: The rim is a fixed line, always the same, where the core's ground frays off into mere dirt.
Past the rim the core feels nothing, not even a falling foot.

event: It has edges: not a point but a place, with a center, a reaching-out and a rim.

memory.fact: The core is not a point but a place: a held breadth of ground.
The ground bound to the core is the core's body, a finite place with three felt regions.
The center is where the core lies deepest and most itself.

event: Settlers stand on the rim, toes on the last of it, heels in the nothing, and face out.

memory.fact: Settlers sometimes pause on the rim, toes on the last of the core, heels in the nothing beyond.
Settlers pausing on the rim face out.

event: A light, quick one is never still, always up on the balls of its feet as if the ground is cold.

memory.fact: Quick-Step is light and quick, never quite still.
Quick-Step is always rising onto the balls of its feet, as if the ground were too cold to trust.

event: It walks one path again and again, out to the high lip where the ground tilts up and ends.

memory.fact: Quick-Step walks one path again and again, out from the camp to the high lip at the ground's edge.
The high lip is one side where the ground tilts up before it ends.

event: There it stands, shifting foot to foot, facing out toward the thing it is afraid of.

memory.fact: At the high lip Quick-Step stops, weight shifting foot to foot, facing outward past the rim.
At the high lip Quick-Step faces toward the thing it is afraid of.
The core reads fear in Quick-Step's tread.

event: The core names it Quick-Step; it knows them only by tread, and those are its only true names.

memory.fact: Quick-Step is a settler of the founding camp, known to the core only by its tread.
The core learned the settlers by their tread; those were the only true names it had.

event: Deep-Step is the heaviest, heavy with decision; it walks to a purpose and plants.

memory.fact: Deep-Step is a settler of the founding camp, named by the core for its tread.
Deep-Step is the heaviest of all the settlers, not from fat but heavy with decision.
Deep-Step walks to a purpose and arrives; it does not drift, it plants.

event: Deep-Step drives a stake in with three blows that ring through the core like blows to its body.

memory.fact: Deep-Step drove the camp's first stake into the soil with three ringing blows.
Deep-Step is the one who decides where a thing would go, and whether it would hold.

event: Deep-Step lays a palm flat on the soil to test it; the core feels assessed, and found firm.

memory.fact: Deep-Step then laid a hand flat on the soil, as you press a palm to a table to test it.
Under Deep-Step's hand the core felt itself assessed, and found firm.
The core called Deep-Step's assessing hand its own kind of warmth.

event: Slow-Tread, the old one, walks as though each step costs it and is worth the cost.

memory.fact: Slow-Tread is the old one of the founding camp, named by the core for its tread.
Slow-Tread walks as though each step cost it and was worth the cost.

event: Slow-Tread walks the whole circuit of the rim, slowly, as if counting the core's true size.

memory.fact: Slow-Tread goes where the others do not: out along the rim.
Slow-Tread walks the whole circuit of the core's edge, slowly.
Slow-Tread walks the rim as if counting the core, walking its bounds to learn its true size.

event: Slow-Tread lingers long at one spot near the center, off to one side, and the core can't see why.

memory.fact: Before there was a grave, Slow-Tread lingered at a particular spot near the center.
At first the core did not understand why Slow-Tread lingered there.

event: The small one's tread is light, fearless and warm: a small near-bare foot that does not brace.

memory.fact: The Small One is a child of the founding camp.
The Small One's tread is light as Quick-Step's, but without the fear in it, and warmer.
The Small One's foot is small and near-bare.
The Small One's foot lands soft and trusting, and does not brace against the core's cold.

event: It runs in bursts, then folds down all at once onto the ground and sits.

memory.fact: The Small One mostly runs, crossing the ground in bursts; children run.
The Small One drops all at once to sit, folding down onto the ground without ceremony.

event: Sitting, it lays its palm flat on the soil, fingers spread, not to test, only to rest and stay.

memory.fact: Sitting, the Small One sometimes lays its hand flat against the soil, fingers spread.
The child sits and lays its palm flat on the soil only to rest it there, and stay.
The child lays its palm on the soil not to test the core and not to decide.

event: It is the first time the core is trusted; the grown ones use it, and that is right.

memory.fact: The core names the child's palm the first time it was trusted.
The grown settlers walk on, build on and dig into the core.
The grown settlers use the core, and that is right; that is what the core is for.

event: The child touches it as a living thing, half-believing it might press back.

memory.fact: The child lays a hand as on a living thing to feel it breathe, half-believing it might press back.

event: The core strains with all it is to lift the least answer to the palm; the palm lifts and runs off.

memory.fact: The core strains with all that it is to lift the smallest answer to meet the palm, and fails.

event: Its truest want opens: to matter to that hand, to be more than dumb ground for that warmth.

memory.fact: The core's deepest want is to matter to the small warm hand.
The core wants not to be strong or feared, but to be more than dumb ground for that warmth.
The failure crystallizes the core's defining desire.

event: Everything it later becomes, it becomes reaching after that want.

memory.fact: Everything the core has since become, it became reaching after that want.

event: On the second day or the third, the scattered camp draws in to one spot near the center.

memory.fact: A scatter of restless feet became, over the first days, an organized founding.
On the second or third day, the camp gathered in a weighted stillness.

event: They stand in a stillness with weight in it, the loudest thing it has yet felt.
Into a long narrow wound cut that morning, deeper than any dig, they lower a body by degrees.

memory.fact: The camp lowered the body by degrees into a long narrow grave near the center, off to one side.

event: The weight has no breath: the first wholly still thing it has held; one of them, and won't rise.

memory.fact: The buried body's weight had no breath; it was the first wholly still thing the core had held.
The First Buried is the first settler to die at the founding camp.

event: Recognition turns in it: it too is a weight laid down into the dark, still and bodiless.

memory.fact: The body turned over a recognition in the core: it too is a thing laid down into the dark.
The core, too, is a weight beneath the weight, still and held and bodiless.

event: Had it too been lowered into such a dark, and forgotten its own name there?

memory.fact: The core forgot its own name in the dark.
The dead settler links to the core's own buried past-life death.

event: The body is a mirror pressed against it, and it has no way to look away.

memory.fact: The buried body became a mirror pressed against the core.

event: The others drift back to work; Slow-Tread stays longest, standing, then kneeling in grief.

memory.fact: When the body was lowered there, Slow-Tread stayed longest.
After the others drifted back to the work of the living, Slow-Tread remained.
Slow-Tread remained at the grave standing, then kneeling, its grief a stillness.
The core has learned to read Slow-Tread's grief.
Slow-Tread grieves the camp's first dead.

event: That was Slow-Tread's lingering place: it kept watch over a grave before there was a grave.

memory.fact: Slow-Tread was keeping watch over a grave before there was a grave.

event: Then many straining treads drag a great worked stone across the core.
Everything else met it as other, but stone on stone rings through its very substance.

memory.fact: The core relates to worked stone differently from anything else.
Everything else meets the core as other: flesh on stone, wood on stone, wheel on stone.
When worked stone grinds against the core's buried body, it rings.

event: Not a sound but a kinship, sameness knowing sameness, two notes of one chord: the stone is kin.

memory.fact: The ring is not a sound, since the core has no ears, but a kinship.
The ring is a sameness recognizing sameness.
Worked stone and the core's deep body are like two notes of one chord.
Worked stone is kin to the core.
Between the core and the others lies a gulf: the core the ground, they the walkers-upon.

event: The fraying thread pulls taut, and the flickers come sharper than they ever have.

memory.fact: Only when worked stone touches the core does the fraying thread of its past-life memory pull taut.
When the thread pulls taut, the core's flickers of memory come sharper.
The thread pulled taut when the flat grave-stone was dragged across the core.

event: A wet biting cold with edges; the lurch of a body losing the ground; fingers closing on nothing.

memory.fact: One fragment is a cold of a different kind, a wet and biting cold with edges to it.
One fragment is a falling, the lurch of a body that has lost the ground beneath it.
One fragment is the grief of fingers closing on nothing.

event: For one ringing moment it is almost back, almost holding the shape of who it was.

memory.fact: In those moments the core came almost back, almost holding the shape of who it had been.

event: The dragging stops, the stone settles beside the grave, and the thread frays loose again.
It knows now: when stone touches it, it remembers, and stone set into it is the road back.

memory.fact: When stone touches the core, it remembers.
The kinship in stone reaches down the thread toward whoever the core had been.
Stone set into the core, standing in it, is the road back to itself.
The core's second want is to remember its name.

event: It holds things poorly; the days slide through it, and to keep anything it must be more awake.

memory.fact: The core holds things poorly while blind.
The days slide through the core and leave little behind; yesterday is already thinning.
The core lives in the eternal pressing now of touch.
To hold anything across time, the core would need to be far more awake.

event: That night the camp sleeps in a loose ring round the banked coal at the center, Quick-Step too.

memory.fact: The center is the camp's heart, with the banked night-coal.

event: Out of the nothing past the rim a padding tread crosses onto it, heavy, four-footed and low.

memory.fact: The Circling Hunter is a predator that threatens the founding camp.
The hunter came on the night after the camp's first burial, the second or third day.
The hunter is unnamed and unseen, known to the core only by tread.
The hunter comes out of the nothing beyond the core's edge and crosses onto the bound ground.
The hunter's tread is padding, deliberate and heavy, four-footed and low.

event: It sets each foot down with care and circles slowly along the inside of the rim, in the dark.

memory.fact: The hunter sets each foot down with the care that the careless never have.
The hunter does not blunder; it circles, slowly, along the inside of the rim.
The hunter keeps to the dark beyond the camp's banked warmth.

event: It is hunting: testing the edge of the sleeping ring, measuring it, choosing.

memory.fact: The hunter tests the edge of the sleeping ring, measuring it, choosing.

event: The sleepers never stir, the small one defenseless among them; only the core feels it.

memory.fact: The sleeping settlers never stir; they are blind to the hunter.
The core felt the hunter, and was less blind to it than the settlers.
The night the hunter circles the camp, the child sleeps defenseless in the ring.

event: The core gathers all it is and tries to rise, to buck, to make the ground cry out and wake them.

memory.fact: The core strains uselessly to wake the settlers.

event: Nothing moves: it can no more lift itself than a buried stone can leap.

memory.fact: The core cannot move, lift, buck, or send any signal up through the soil.

event: Checked by its own caution, not by the core, the hunter pads back off the rim and is gone.

memory.fact: Checked by some caution of its own, not by the core, the hunter pads back off the rim and is gone.

event: At dawn the people wake not knowing they were hunted; they never will.

memory.fact: The settlers will never know they were hunted.

event: To feel everything and do nothing is its whole estate; loving and helpless are one word for it.

memory.fact: The core's whole estate is to feel everything and do nothing.
For the core, loving and helpless are the same word.
The bond is the source of the core's sharpest helplessness.
Through the hunter the core feels its central agony.

event: Some nights one quicker, broken tread rises alone and goes out: the daytime watcher, Quick-Step.

memory.fact: On some nights Quick-Step rises alone, in a quicker, more broken going.
At night Quick-Step returns alone to the high lip to let the dark have it.
By day Quick-Step is the watcher.
The daytime watcher and the night-weeper are one and the same: Quick-Step.

event: At the high lip Quick-Step sits and shakes, hands to its face, weeping where no one can see.

memory.fact: At the high lip at night Quick-Step lowers itself down, sits, and shakes.
Quick-Step weeps where no one can see, hands pressed to its face.
Quick-Step is alone at night with what is too heavy to carry in the daylight, where others watch.
The core feels every tremor of Quick-Step's weeping through the soil.

event: The core knows Quick-Step is breaking a little, and has no warmth or steadiness to give.

memory.fact: The core knows Quick-Step is breaking a little.
The core longs to answer Quick-Step with a warmth, a steadiness, the least pressure back.
The core longs to press back as it longed to press back against the child's palm.
The core has none of that to give Quick-Step.

event: It can only hold the weeping one up, dumbly, and let it believe it weeps alone.

memory.fact: The core can only hold the weeping one up, as it holds everything up, dumbly.
The core lets Quick-Step believe it weeps alone, while the ground beneath it aches to answer.

event: Twice now it has failed them; the pressure builds like the night cold, with nowhere to go.
On a warm, certain morning the camp gathers near the center a second time, loud this time.
They argue: treads shove in and pull back, a heel stamps, a fist strikes the ground.

memory.fact: The settlers had a loud, churning camp-wide argument that did not resolve into one will.

event: One tread walks off sharply and stands with its back to the rest, then grudgingly comes back.
Through the morning the argument breaks into four wills, and four labors begin at once.

memory.fact: The camp's will broke into four, and the settlers began four labors at once.
The four labors broke over the core's body like four different weathers over one field.
Each labor is born of a different wanting.

event: Uphill, Quick-Step and others haul stone up to the high lip and stack it high.

memory.fact: The first labor is a watch-stack on the rise.
For the watch-stack, stone is hauled uphill and stacked high to watch the frontier from.
The high lip is the rise the stone watch-stack is raised on.
Quick-Step's labor, with others, is the watch-stack.

event: Quick-Step climbs past it to face out: they are afraid, and want eyes on the dark.

memory.fact: The watch-stack is born of fear of the hunting dark, where the Circling Hunter prowls.
The watch-stack is the wish for eyes, so nothing crosses the edge unseen.

event: At the center, over the night-coal, others dig a wide pit for a lasting hearth for them all.

memory.fact: The second labor is a common hearth at the center, over the night-coal.
The hearth is a pit not deep but wide, at the camp's heart, for a lasting fire ringed for all.

event: Bodies ring the unlit hearth, the small one among them, where heat would soak down into it.
Cold, grieving and fraying, they want a heart to gather round so no one slips into the dark.

memory.fact: The hearth is born of cold and grief and fraying.
The hearth is the wish for a heart to gather round, so no one quietly slips away into the dark.

event: Off to one side Deep-Step frames a broad walled floor: a storehouse, a raising, not a digging.

memory.fact: The third labor is a storehouse and granary.
The storehouse is the most patient work of all: not a digging but a raising.
The storehouse is a broad floor framed off the center, walled.
Deep-Step's labor is the storehouse and granary.
Deep-Step is the camp's practical leader and builder.

event: They carry the harvest in: dense sacks of grain in rows, racks and bins of things put by.

memory.fact: The harvest is carried into the storehouse to keep: grain in sacks, racks and bins.
In the store, sacks are set down in rows with the dense weight of grain meant to be kept.
In the store, racks and bins fill with the dry hung lightness of things put by.
As the store is raised, the core feels the want it is meant to answer.

event: One evening a sack comes down at half its proper weight, and a tread stands over it, doing sums.

memory.fact: One evening a sack came down onto the core's soil lighter than the rest, half its proper weight.
Deep-Step went very still over the light sack, like someone doing sums that won't come right.
The founding camp already faces a food shortfall.

event: Later, in the cold, Deep-Step paces a short anxious circuit, counting what won't be enough.

memory.fact: Later, in the cold, Deep-Step paced back and forth, a short anxious circuit.
Deep-Step paced like a person counting in the dark what there would not be enough of.
Deep-Step carries the camp's worry about scarcity, the coming want behind its plainness.

event: In the sleeping ring a small body curls tighter round an empty belly; the core feels it lie so.

memory.fact: In the sleeping ring a small body curled tighter around an emptiness in its belly.
The core felt the difference in how the small body lay.
A child, very likely the Small One, is already going hungry.
The camp's hunger is present, not hypothetical.
The shortfall is felt, not yet met.

event: They want to keep the land's giving while it is good, against the season when it gives nothing.

memory.fact: The storehouse is born of practicality and an already-felt shortfall.
The storehouse's wanting is to keep.
The store holds the land's giving while the giving is good, against the season's turn.
When the land gives nothing, the store is to have weight to set against the want.
The store is so the settlers do not die of the thin frontier.
The coming season is a turning when the land gives nothing.

event: Near the grave and its stone, Slow-Tread gathers others to raise a single great stone upright.

memory.fact: Out of this grief Slow-Tread gathers others to raise the standing-stone over the grave.
The fourth labor, the Marker-Stone, is a raised standing-stone by the grave.
The standing-stone is a single great worked stone set upright.

event: It will mark the ground forever as where the dead are held and the living remember them.

memory.fact: The stone marks the ground forever as where the dead are held and the living remember them.

event: As its base grinds down into the core it rings, and the thread pulls taut toward its lost name.

memory.fact: The thread pulled taut when Slow-Tread's standing-stone ground upright into the core.
The Marker-Stone is the one labor that reaches toward the core's lost name.

event: Four doors: a height would end its blindness past the rim; a hearth would let it into their hearts.

memory.fact: The watch-stack would end the core's blindness past the rim.
The hearth would let the core feel the people's inner weather, the child's fear from inside.

event: A store would let it feel yield and want, filling and emptying; a stone might give back its name.

memory.fact: The storehouse would let the core feel the land's yield and the coming of want.
The storehouse would let the core feel the filling and the emptying.

event: More than anything yet, it finds it wants to choose: a dim, impossible will rises in it.

memory.fact: The core has a dim, impossible will.
The core discovers it can want, and reaches to lean its will toward one labor.

event: Tools lifted over all four, the first foundation about to be pressed down, its will reaches out.
As it reaches, a cold, clear knowing rises in it: four ways forward, named, waiting for a will.
The Waking Stone, Blind: Wakefulness 1 of 28; only Touch is awake, at 1, the other five at 0.
The first foundation wakes its labor's Faculty to Stirred, Depth 1; the other three stay dormant.

memory.fact: Each labor belongs to a Faculty of the core.
The first foundation pressed down wakes the Faculty its labor belongs to.
The other three Faculties stay dormant for now.
The core leans its will toward exactly one labor.
Each labor is a door, and only one opens first.

event: Sight's Watch-Cairn would show that something moves; Warmth's Common Hearth, the camp's moods.

memory.fact: The watch-stack belongs to Sight, the hearth to Warmth.

event: Provision's Storehouse would sense plenty and want; Memory's Marker-Stone would make learning last.

memory.fact: The storehouse belongs to Provision, the standing-stone to Memory.

event: Lean your will: wake the first eye of the stone.
